newsitem.title: USA: Amsouth says new revs, cost control spur Q1.
newsitem.headline: Amsouth says new revs, cost control spur Q1.

text.p: AmSouth Bancorp said Tuesday its first quarter earnings increased 18.1 percent over last year largely due to a combination of revenue growth and cost containment.
The regional bank holding company earlier reported earnings of $0.98 per share for the first quarter ending March 31, versus $$0.83 during the same quarter last year.
It reported net income of $54.6 million for the first quarter, a 15.7 percent increase over the 1996 quarter.
"Our improved performance continues to be driven by solid revenue growth coupled with cost containment," said C. Dowd Ritter, AmSouth Bancorp chairman.

The company said net interest income increased 6.0 percent compared with the first quarter of 1996. "This reflects the shift in the mix of earning assets from investment securities to higher yielding loans," it said in a prepared statement.
It said average loans, net of unearned income, excluding residential first mortgages, increased 12.9 percent over the 1996 quarter.
The provision for loan losses increased $2.6 million in the first quarter from $15.1 million in the same period a year ago, AmSouth said.
